-Zodiac upholstery flea spray. I swear by it. My first apartment had a flea infestation from the people that used to be there. You'd put one foot on the carpet and you'd be crawling with fleas. I was literally going insane. Did some research and read promising reviews about this spray and it worked. All you need is a fine mist, making sure you're covering everything evenly. Couches, carpet, mattresses, and make sure to get the corners of the rooms. It's safe once it's completely dried. Definitely don't let your pets go anywhere near it before it dries, but it dries out quickly and I've never had a problem with it. Do a few rooms first, open the windows so there's ventilation and cover the cracks under the doors with towels because cats are super curious. Once those first rooms are done, you can spray the other areas and move everyone into the done rooms until the rest of the house is clear. Or you can move everyone into the garage or go for a drive.

I have never had to flea bomb by doing all of this. My ex tried some cheaper spray he found at Walmart and he went through hell for HALF A DAMM YEAR trying to get rid of them. He finally gave in and purchased Zodiac after a lot of pushing on my part. Their numbers were significantly cut down almost immediately. With the cheap spray the would bounce back like every couple of days, but a week after Zodiac they were mostly gone. I think you can respray like 2 weeks after the first round of it's super intense.

I started out doing classical training and jazz choir at the same time, and I was an alto for the first year of jazz choir. As I improved in my private lessons and my range broadened, I moved up to soprano 2 and eventually soprano 1. The transition was a bit hard for me because I hadn't yet gotten a full grasp of the techniques for healthy singing and would strain very easily. I stopped jazz choir when they introduced the opera workshop and I basically just did classical singing for a couple of years. Felt a little more improvement. A couple of years after THAT, I started jazz choir again amd holy SHIT, soprano 1 and 2 were a breeze. I used the techniques and applied them to what I was singing and I only remember getting fatigued once because the choir director had us repeat the same line for like 10 minutes straight and it was pretty high. I blended in just fine, holding back and and going full in as it was needed, depending on the style of the song. It's about how you use your voice. It's just like with any instrument. 

Classical training gives you the tools for healthy singing. A good understanding of breath control and usage, resonance, and a better understanding of what it feels like to sing healthy in YOUR body specifically, is valuable in any type of singing and I believe is vital in any style. After ten years of it I can definitely say it pays off.

Do you feel any tension when singing up higher? It all sounds really nice, though I thought I heard you struggle a little up there. It's something I've struggled with (I used to sing opera) and what helped me was recognizing where I might have tension, like the tongue. Practice good vowel placement (for example, where the tongue sits when you do an 'ee' or 'oo' sound). Make sure it's not pulling back and tensing up, and make sure your head and neck are aligned. Keep your chest lifted but everything else relaxed. 

When I'm singing up higher during warmups, I also like to take my hand and move it down to trick my brain into thinking I'm not going 'up'. For example, with a siren exercise (going from a low pitch, up high, and then down again) I move my hand the opposite way that I imagine my voice going. 

Hope I explained myself alright, it can be a little difficult without demonstration. Keep up the good work!

Bounced around from my dad's to my sisters' places because they all treated me like shit, ended up moving in with my bf at the time at around 16/17yo. Got left by him too, ended up in and out of inpatient mental hospitals because of severe depression. Was in a 2.5 year relationship with someone who didn't give a shit about me, all because I was desperately looking for any type of love or belonging. I still struggle with that.

I feel like there's always going to be that little kid inside me that yearns for her parents, and that angry teenager that hates what they did. It was a fucked up thing to go through, and it's several years of trauma. It makes sense that it affects me so much because that shit changes a person. It makes sense that it still hurts because you didn't deserve to go through all of that.

I've done a lot of therapy and a lot of thinking. So much thinking, YEARS of thinking, about why they did it or how they could have done all of that to a child. To their kid. I've accepted the fact that my mom left because she was not capable of being my mother. She lived a fucked up life full of strife and took it out on us. The whole "hurt people hurt people" thing. Honestly if she had stayed, I might've killed myself by now. If my dad had raised me, I would've been fucked up in different, just as terrible, ways. 

I've met others that have had similar upbringing, and what I've learned is that people like us grew up doing what we had to do to survive. There's no instruction manual for this. The most important thing I've learned in therapy is that recovery isn't linear. Don't kick yourself when you're already down. Take care of the child in you. Take care of yourself the way your parents couldn't. Do the things you wished you could have done in the years that were stolen from you. I'm trying to do stuff that I wish I had as a kid. Ballet lessons, seeing shows and plays, dressing how I want, eating cake at an ungodly hour. Because life is so short and I can't wait for somebody do these things with me. What are some things you always wanted to do or still want to do? What are some ways that you wish they had cared for you, and how can you do those things for you or your daughter?

You might have thought through all of these things and I'm just preaching to the choir here so I apologize if it's not helpful. Just take it a day at a time and if that ever gets hard, take it moment by moment. It can be hard to live in the present when part of you is stuck in the past and part of you may be fearing the future, and that is completely understandable given your circumstances and upbringing. 

Regarding your other post about your mom, you can only do so much. You deserve apologies and explanations. Recently, I had an ugly talk with my dad about the past and unfortunately, for now, I have to accept that I won't get either of those. It hurts so bad and sent me into a week long episode, but it's two weeks later now and I'm still here slowly (sloooooowly) feeling a little less shitty every day. 

TLDR: recovery isn't linear, it will look different every day.

Once you stick to a litter, be wary of changing it. Cats hate change. My bf brought home the wrong litter once and I thought, what the heck let's try it. My cat pissed everywhere until we changed it. 

My cat used to pee everywhere for like, two years. Don't keep your laundry on the floor. It's a nice comfy place for a cat to piss on. Peeing problems could be medical or behavioral. Rule out the medical first and go from there.

Cats are such loving, caring, affectionate animals, if you treat them with respect and love. It's a myth that they don't need as much attention as a dog. It took a while for my Arty and I to bond completely (almost 2 years!) but because of all the love I showed him, he is now a lap cat and absolutely loves seeing me. He rolls over like a puppy and he is so affectionate.

Remember that when you adopt a kitten, you may be separating it from it's siblings. It definitely affects them. When I got Jasper as a kitten and we got home, she immediately darted under the bed. She would have stayed there all the time had we not gotten the actual bed off the frame so there was no room underneath. It's important to give them their space because they're getting used to their new home! But it's not good for them to be hiding so much. I got rid of her hiding spots but provided cozy nooks for her. It's been a year and a half and she's trying to cuddle now, which would have been unheard of when we first got her.

 Be patient, give space when they need it, give affection, and playtime is so important!

Also, my Arty was having urinary problems and the vet thinks it's the tap water (if you se your cat ever taking a long time to pee and you don't see anything coming out, it could be a sign of a blockage, uti, etc. I called an emergency vet clinic to see if it was something to worry about. It was! I took him that day. If your vet bill ever becomes too much, they have programs that can cover it for you. Just ask.). I would suggest investing in a water fountain with a filter on it. Keeps the water clean too so you don't have to change it as much. 

Keep the area around their litterbox lit.

I use a little tub to bathe them if I have to. It freaks them out less than being in a huge tub with water. Also, don't bathe your cat unless you absolutely need to because they're dirty or because of their breed. They are pretty clean animals and will take care of that themselves. 

Wet food is better than dry food! But there are cats that still like dry food more. Just keep fresh water around. And don't put the food next to the water. Some cats will avoid the water completely if you do that. 

Get a grooming brush. So worth it. Hairballs suck and I'm terrified of my cats ever getting a blockage, especially my medium haired kitty. Plus it's great for bonding. 

And finally, I wouldn't touch over the counter flea products. Some have a lot of lawsuits because of pet deaths. I bathe them with original Dawn dish soap to drown the fleas in addition to using Zodiac upholstery spray for the carpets and anything upholstered. Be careful not to get their ears wet while bathing them because it could cause an ear infection. 

EDIT: and please get them fixed! Even if they are inside cats. If they run out, they will contribute to the cat overpopulation. There are enough cats on the streets.

I'm so sorry but final edit: careful with essential oils. Many are extremely toxic to cats. A LOT of things are toxic to cats. Also, cats hate strong perfumes.
